title: Polynomial-time split search with bounded space
statement: For all natural numbers $C$ and $e$, there exist a finite Turing machine $M$ and a natural number $c$ such that, on every Boolean input $w$ of length $n$, $M$ halts within $c(n+1)^{e+2}$ steps and outputs the encoding that doubles each bit of the prefix of $w$ of length $i$, appends $01$, and then appends the remaining suffix, where $i$ is the least integer in $0,\ldots,n$ satisfying $i+C(i+1)^e=n$; if no such $i$ exists, its output is the empty word. For every Boolean word $x$ and every time $t$, the computation of $M$ on $x$ up to time $t$ uses at most $c(|x|+1)^{e+1}$ work-tape cells.
